name: libpano
desc: Build panoramic images from a set of overlapping images
why: Stitches overlapping photos into panoramas; a real image-geometry transform, though the library is quite plumbing-like.

brief.what_it_is: libpano13 (the Panorama Tools library, called pano13 in the README) is a backend C library for stitching overlapping photographs into panoramas. Its input is a set of overlapping source images plus control-point and projection data. Its output is a stitched panoramic image. The page says it is the backend used by many applications, and it ships with command-line tools: PToptimizer for optimising control points, panoinfo for querying the library version, PTmender as a replacement for PTStitcher, PTblender for colour and brightness correction, PTtiff2psd for converting TIFFs to a PSD, and PTuncrop for converting cropped TIFFs to normal TIFFs.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames Panorama Tools as the shared engine behind a family of panorama front ends (Hugin, PTGui, PTMac and others), so that the stitching maths lives in one library. The page is a legacy project page, with its last update dated 13 May 2013.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives no algorithm detail. It says most front ends call the PTStitcher tool to do the actual stitching, and that PTmender is a replacement for PTStitcher. It also says the library is the backend that front ends and tools call into.

commands_seen.context: Fetches the libpano13 development source code from the Mercurial repository on SourceForge. The page gives this as the basic instruction for downloading the pano13 library source.

brief.install_notes: Most users do not need to build it: the page says Hugin usually ships with a recent version of the library and command-line tools, so downloading Hugin is the easy route. A Windows installer with the library, command-line tools and Photoshop plugins is available from Jim Watters' site, and an OS X bundle is linked from the page. For the latest code you must compile from source, which needs Mercurial (Windows users must install a Mercurial client first). The page says compiling instructions are in the source and may be out of date for your platform. No runtime or account is mentioned.
brief.standout: It is the shared engine underneath many panorama tools, and it has a deliberate, documented limit: the source caps fisheye input at fields of view of 160 degrees or less, because of possible US patents on fisheye stitching. The page also notes that the PTStitcher tool most front ends use has no available source code, which is why the open replacements PTmender and Hugin's nona exist.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release listed is libpano13-2.9.18 (2 May 2011). The most recent news item is 13 May 2013, about SourceForge moving repositories. Nothing on the page dates later than that. The page is a legacy SourceForge site, and the README points to the Launchpad bug tracker and the PanoTools wiki for ongoing work.
brief.caveats: Several things on the page are dated: development moved from SVN to Mercurial in 2011, and the 2013 note says some repositories moved. The fisheye field-of-view cap of 160 degrees is built into the source. The README says the compile instructions may be out of date for some platforms. The library is low-level, with no GUI of its own. The page points to a separate Hugin GUI and to front ends. Licensing: the page says all files on the site are under the GNU General Public License. The Brew caveats field was empty, and the scout notes describe it as plumbing-like.
quotes: pano13 is the name of the library (like lotus123 or XFree86) not the version (which is currently 2.9.18).
